In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conservation of resources (COR) theory has been applied in a sales context for the first time.
the conservation of resources perspective provides an excellent explanation of why people make the attributions they do in the face of a setback.
the COR model is a useful and powerful theoretical model for explaining the salesperson’s response to a sales failure, particularly in terms of attributional processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sales failure attributions are not only a function of the failure experience itself but are also a function of the resources available to the individual to deal with the setback.
the COR perspective is a useful lens for examining how salespeople make attributions for their sales setbacks.
salespeople who experience a sales setback will conserve their resources by making external attributions when the sales setback has high failure impact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
salespeople are motivated to protect their resources and will use attributions to do so.

when salespeople experience a loss in their sales performance, they are more likely to attribute this to external causes when the loss is perceived as having a large negative impact on their resources (e.g., time, money, energy, etc.).

salespeople who experience a sales setback that is perceived as having a high impact (e.g., a large amount of sales was lost or the salesperson was unable to meet a goal) will be more likely to use external attributions to explain the cause of their failure.
